policy: Each row: the decision, what we ALREADY KNOW (with measured values and sources), what we DO NOT KNOW, and how the missing information could be discovered (linked to suggestions). No decision below should be made until its unknowns are resolved or consciously accepted.

decisions.question: May any strategy be promoted from paper toward live staking?
we_know: All four implementable strategies FAIL the promotion gates (best: STRAT-TOTAL-3, 4/8 gates; beat-close 50.31%, permutation p=0.45, CI includes 50%) — engine/gates_evaluation.json
The model's spread disagreement has NEGATIVE line value (beat-close 41.8%, CI [39.8%,43.8%]) — the closing market outperforms this model on sides (data/leaderboard.json)
Flat-stake ROI is negative on every staked strategy (side −21.9%, total −4.5%, parlay −58.8%) (data/leaderboard.json)
Rewards awarded to date: 0 — consistent with every prior session's finding
we_do_not_know: Whether injury/depth integration (the tracker now quantifies replacement depth) can produce a strategy that beats the close — untested (SUG-M7)
Whether a better model class (market-aware residuals rather than pure Elo) would have positive line value — untested
Live CLV behavior: all evidence is archival; no live origination-with-timestamp record exists yet (SUG-M4)
how_to_discover: SUG-M7 pre-register an injury-adjusted signal and measure it forward
SUG-M4 begin timestamped live origination so CLV becomes measurable honestly
Re-run the gate evaluation after each week; promotion stays blocked until MG-5/6/7/8 all pass

decisions.question: What bankroll, staking and reward structure applies IF a strategy ever passes the gates?
we_know: The leaderboard's rewarded tier exists but nothing has ever qualified (gates all fail; rewards=0)
Staking metrics assume flat 1-unit stakes at standard −110 pricing — an ASSUMPTION, flagged (no official odds archive exists)
we_do_not_know: The owner's risk tolerance, bankroll size, and whether real staking is ever intended
Which reward form applies: track-record badges, promotion ladder, or something else
how_to_discover: Owner decision required — cannot be discovered from data
SUG-M3/SUG-M4 establish the measurement layer a reward policy would need

decisions.question: Is the labelled third-party line archive an acceptable market benchmark?
we_know: No official source for betting lines exists anywhere (the NFL does not publish prices) — every market number in this repo is labelled THIRD-PARTY (FLAG-M1)

The archive's conventions were verified empirically this session: spread_line = expected home margin (7+ point favorites win outright 81.7%/77.2%, n=1608; per-season mean(line−result) within ±1.9); closing-archive settlement agreement 99.8% excl pushes (n=3808)
Opening numbers: 2013-2020 archived without capture times (behave near-close, mean |Δ| 0.92 pts); 2021 Westgate opens archived; 2022+ opens absent
we_do_not_know: The exact capture time of any archived line (source does not publish it)
Whether a rights-cleared price vendor would materially change backtest conclusions
how_to_discover: SUG-M4: capture opens with timestamps from the next slate onward
Accept labelled third-party (recommended: conventions verified) or block all line comparisons — reviewer's call

decisions.question: What correlation cap should govern same-game prop combinations?
we_know: Cross-game leg dependence is MEASURED: same-week legs both cover 23.8% observed vs 25.0% market-implied expectation — gap −1.19pp (SE 0.26pp, n=27,129 pairs, 269 weeks): cross-game parlays are marginally worse than independence assumes (data/correlations.json CT-2)
Same-game prop correlations CANNOT be computed: no prop results source exists (SUG-M2)
we_do_not_know: Any same-game prop correlation value (blank by rule — never inferred)
The cap value itself: cannot be set without measured correlations
how_to_discover: SUG-M2 first, then re-run the dependence machinery on prop legs
Until then the rule is: same-game prop combos are NOT priced and NOT staked in this namespace

decisions.question: Is the replacement-depth weighting (2nd=1.0, 3rd=1.5, 4th=2.0, none=2.5) the right convention?
we_know: The tracker quantifies depth of replacement for 8 teams (10 starter-out rows: 7 replaced by 2nd string, 3 by NONE) — data/replacement_depth.json
The weights are THIS REPO'S convention, published openly, not derived from any official number (FLAG-M6/M-7)
we_do_not_know: Whether these weights predict anything (no outcome calibration has been run)
Whether depth charts themselves predict outcomes better than raw injury counts
how_to_discover: Validate empirically: regress market line moves (open→close, archived) on the deficiency index — measurable from data already in the repo
SUG-M5 extends coverage before drawing any conclusion from 8 teams

decisions.question: Which namespace is the single source of truth for NFL facts?
we_know: Twenty-plus NFL namespaces exist; SIX now implement overlapping versions of the same eight requirements (nfl-markets this session, plus peer sessions' nfl-market, nfl-price-snapshot, nfl-core, nfl-marketboard, nfl-ledger) — all merged and linked in the root navigation (superset preserved)
This session's differentiator: the only store POPULATED with archived opening/closing numbers (12,573 snapshot rows) + a 4,056-row verified results feed + counterfactually-exercised demotion gate
we_do_not_know: The owner's preference among the six candidate stores — D-1 (nfl-core's page) and SUG-M3 (this namespace) both propose a choice; a one-line decision resolves it
how_to_discover: SUG-M3 proposes nfl-markets as the store of record with nfl-ledger as schema owner — a reviewer can accept, amend, or reject in one line
